name: Fairmont Taghazout Bay
positioning: Beachfront Fairmont resort on Morocco's Atlantic coast at Taghazout, with a spa, several restaurants and bars, and private villas.
best_for: Families who want a kids' club, a playground and a teen space
Guests who want a beach resort with surfing classes, golf and a spa

facts.text: The resort has direct beach access.
Rooms have private balconies and marble bathrooms.
Rooms combine contemporary design with a touch of Berber heritage.
The villas come with butler services.
Beef and Reef is a surf-and-turf restaurant beside the resort's palm-lined infinity pool.
Nola is a speakeasy-style bar at the resort with a whiskey collection and Cuban cigars.
The resort heats its pool with a solar-powered system and recycles greywater for property irrigation.
The resort offers surfing classes, golf, a spa and cultural excursions.
The resort has a Fun4Kidz Club and a playground for younger guests, and a teen space called Le Hangout.

highlights.text: Condé Nast Traveler describes it as the first luxury resort to debut in the former fishing village of Taghazout.
Morimoto Taghazout Bay is a restaurant at the resort that serves sushi platters and dishes such as beef tataki.
The resort's villas each have a private garden and a heated infinity pool.
The spa facilities include a sauna, jacuzzi, hammam and magnesium pool.

considerations.text: Taghazout town center is a 30-minute walk from the resort along the beachfront promenade.
The resort sits on the Atlantic coast ten miles north of Agadir.
WhataHotel notes the location is remote and requires travel from major cities.

sources.title: Fairmont Taghazout Bay review, Condé Nast Traveler
